column4: The section names the root w-j-d for finding a lost camel; this verse repeatedly has Zakariyya find provision with Mary in her sanctuary, making finding an act of sustenance for someone under care.

The section makes the orphan's delayed care visible; this neighboring inheritance verse tells guardians to consider the weak descendants they may leave behind, extending the orphan's vulnerability to dependents after a death.
The section names livestock as النعم because of their good; this verse distinguishes cattle for carrying from those for other uses and tells people to eat from God's provision.
The section develops shelter and provision for a vulnerable wanderer; this verse says God sheltered an oppressed community, strengthened it, and provided good things, آواكم ورزقكم.
The section defines مأوى as a creature's refuge and shows the lost receiving guidance; this verse says God calls to the abode of peace and guides whom He wills to a straight path.

The parallel is limited: the section's lost animal is restored to care, while a caravan discovers Joseph in a well and hides him for sale. This is a specific found-vulnerable-person scene with an exploitative outcome.
After 18:16 tells the youths to take refuge in the cave, this verse describes the sun passing around them and says whoever God guides is guided, joining shelter to divine protection and direction.
The section defines a refuge as a place a creature resorts to; this continuation places the cave youths' dog at the entrance, a concrete animal at the threshold of shelter.
The section follows an animal from loss into a search; here two travelers forget their fish and it slips into the sea, turning loss into the event that begins their search.

The section's owner seeks what went missing; the attendant recalls where the fish was lost at the rock, and 18:64 completes this row's contribution by naming it what they sought and prompting their return.
The section's root w-j-d links finding with the end of a search; Moses recognizes the lost fish's location as what they sought and retraces their steps, turning loss into a guide.
The section says finding the lost can lead to guidance; at the marked location Moses and his attendant find a servant of God and ask to follow him, making the find a meeting with a guide.
The section's dictionary form هادي means the leading animal or guide; this verse calls Abraham's descendants leaders who guide by God's command, connecting headship with directed care.
The section's herd follows its keeper; this verse describes a person who takes his desire as god, and 25:44 completes the contrast by likening such heedlessness to cattle that are more astray.
The section's dictionary form هادي names a leader at the head who leads a herd; this verse reverses that role with leaders who call people to the Fire.

The section's lost camel remains a living creature its owner can seek; this verse uses the section's root ض ل ل for bodies lost into the earth and asks whether they can be created anew, a more final kind of disappearance.
The section's dictionary form هادي names a herd's leader; this verse describes leaders who guide by God's command, making animal direction a model for communal guidance.
The section calls livestock النعم because they are a blessing; this verse names ships and livestock as mounts, grounding that blessing in the animal's use.

The section ends by connecting livestock's name to blessing and the command to speak of God's favor; this verse tells riders to remember their Lord's blessing when mounted and praise the One who subjected the animal.
